rulings.topic: The directional masters were painted for a flat 2D world; they are not views of one 3D object
rulings.ruling: Matt verbatim: "Please think through a potential fundamental problem with the knight.. the E and W frames, maybe also NE and NW were generated/painted to show well on a flat 2D world.. I don't think the master directional frames work for 3D at all.." Conductor analysis (CONFIRMED by this run's own measurements): the 8 approved stills are 2D illustrations with readability cheats, not a turnaround of one object: (a) M-a fit: azimuth steps off by up to -11.5/+9.5 deg on the diagonals, scale spread 8.1%, E stance staggered where S/N are not; (b) the pollaxe was painted at a near-FIXED SCREEN offset and bearing (the blade broadside in both E and S, geometrically impossible for one rigid weapon; no single grip point fits, rms 51 px); (c) the stills are painted at about 20 deg elevation vs the world camera's 53 deg (character drawn flatter than the ground, the classic 2D convention). Consequences already observed: Meshy from the masters lost the axe head and invented the tabard back; the M-b projection paint fragmented; and, likely a root cause of the T1 morph, Astra was given two conflicting truths per frame (the master's cheated look vs the render's true geometry) and alternated between them (the pollaxe head flips fan/flat frame to frame). The manticore, whose reference MC-1 was painted as a neutral model sheet that the model was built from, drifted far less. Rule going forward: (1) masters are STYLE/IDENTITY references only; (2) the source of truth for any 3D-driven route is ONE model sheet made for 3D (orthographic, neutral pose, one scale, weapon separate: KA-1/KP-1/MC-1); (3) every painting over 3D uses views rendered FROM THE MODEL as its look reference (the T5 method), never the per-direction masters; (4) wanted 2D readability cheats (weapon turned broadside, head biased toward camera) become explicit, deterministic per-direction 3D adjustments; (5) the character view angle in true 3D (world camera 53 deg vs the 2D convention of about 20 deg) is a design question for Matt, captured both ways in T7-A.

notes.topic: The T10BF paint driver stalled ~2 h 54 min on the retired 41 GiB guard -- conductor defect
notes.note: R-C9-87 moved the storage gate to 25 GiB and t10bf_drive.sh was edited to -ge 25, but the RUNNING driver was not restarted: zsh had already parsed its while-loop, so the live process kept the old 41 GiB guard. From 03:06:45Z it logged 'DISK GUARD: waiting (<41 GiB)' every 2 min with 33 GiB free (above the real gate). Found 06:00Z while checking the log; stopped and restarted at 06:00:49Z on the current script, which resumed at chunks 3_2 + 1_3 (12 of 16 painted). No work lost, no spend lost; ~3 h of lane time lost. LESSON: editing a script does not change a process already running it -- a gate change is not in force until every process enforcing the old gate is restarted, and the check is the process's own log line, not the file. Same shape as the #75 cl. 6 family: the record changed and the running state did not follow.

notes.topic: RULING (conductor, SCENEWRIGHT): the painting is the world's light and its ink
notes.note: The painter painted over a greybox lit by the scene's own 55 deg sun, so the painted light agrees with the scene light by construction; relighting it lights it twice (mini overlay 15.5 unlit vs 40.7 lit). (1) STATIC painted pieces (the 54 heroes, the painted ground) show their plate as painted: no ramp, no pen (their outline ink is in the plate). (2) DYNAMIC things (him, monsters, particles, the 3D snow's trails, anything that moves) keep the ramp with the same sun and the pen. (3) Where they meet: his cast shadow darkens the painted world; he is darkened inside a painted shadow; static pieces cast NO real shadow onto the painted ground (theirs is painted). (4) The 3D heather moves, so it takes its colour from the painting beneath each spray under the ramp's same sun, judged by the overlay. Why this does not repeat R-C9-72 ('lit, it mostly looks worse'): that painted world's light was freehand and disagreed with his; this painting's light was painted over the scene's own sun.
